read_sources: required local control surfaces and M7_sol review_contract.yaml
one completed non-Zechariah blind literary proposal for format only

non_authority_statement: Candidate literary and structural evidence only. Every unit is LOW confidence and deferred_human_or_external_ai. No theology, identity, history, fulfillment, chronology, canon, authorship, preferred witness, preferred reading, preferred translation, source tradition, graph, retrieval, reviewed-gold, chunk-output, or promotion authority is claimed.
routing_principle: Prefer the larger coherent dated address, night-vision episode, question-and-interpretation exchange, embedded oracle, sign-act, fast-inquiry response, revelation/burden parent, shepherd enactment, lament, refrain-governed oracle sequence, stanza, and formal closure. Chapter edges are used only when a text-internal form closes or restarts there; no chapter fallbacks.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: dated opening return summons and remembered response
macro_parent_alternatives.preservation_reason: The first date and word-event formula open a self-contained exhortation whose repeated return language, questions, and remembered response close before the later night-vision date.
The second date introduces a sustained series shaped by seeing, asking, interpretation, renewed lifting of the eyes, and a final earth-ranging chariot vision echoing the opening patrol.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: night-vision cycle with crowning sign-act appendix
macro_parent_alternatives.preservation_reason: The vision cycle closes at 6:8, while the renewed word-event and crowns form a related appendix with command, memorial, and conditional close.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: dated fast inquiry and extended multi-oracle response
macro_parent_alternatives.preservation_reason: A new regnal date, delegation, and fasting question initiate repeated word-events carrying accusation, assurances, commands, transformed fasts, and a final nations-seeking scene.
The revelation heading opens geographic judgment, royal proclamation, prisoner and flock imagery, restoration speech, lament, and paired shepherd enactments without another burden heading.
A second revelation heading opens an in-that-day sequence of siege, defense, lament, cleansing, shepherd striking, day movement, worship, and all-holy closure.

global_hot_zones.issue: Recurring vision reports, questions, interpretations, embedded oracles, and a final sign-act support both episodes and one cycle parent.
global_hot_zones.handling: Retain episodes while preserving 1:7-6:8 and 1:7-6:15 as larger alternatives.

global_hot_zones.issue: The patrol report turns into angelic lament and an embedded proclamation.
global_hot_zones.handling: Keep the exchange whole because the proclamation answers the patrol scene; decide no historical referent or chronology.

global_hot_zones.issue: The measuring-line vision shifts at 2:6 into a direct come/flee/sing proclamation.
global_hot_zones.handling: Separate at the imperative restart but preserve the complete vision-oracle movement as an alternative.

global_hot_zones.issue: Garment removal closes an enactment before a solemn charge and sign saying.
global_hot_zones.handling: Use the solemn-assurance seam while retaining the whole Joshua scene as a parent alternative; decide no identity.

global_hot_zones.issue: The lampstand vision embeds two word-events before returning to olive-tree questions.
global_hot_zones.handling: Keep the whole interlocked vision; record smaller alternatives without assigning identity.

global_hot_zones.issue: The final chariot vision closes at 6:8 and a renewed word-event starts a sign-act at 6:9.
global_hot_zones.handling: Separate at the word-event while preserving a cycle-plus-appendix alternative.

global_hot_zones.issue: The fasting question receives several restarted word-events rather than one compact answer.
global_hot_zones.handling: Use internal word-event and refrain seams while preserving the full inquiry-response parent.

global_hot_zones.issue: Poetry, prose enactment, shifting pronouns, shepherd imagery, and direct speech create many seams under one heading.
global_hot_zones.handling: Respect stanza, speech, lament, and sign-act changes while preserving the first-revelation parent; infer no speaker identity, history, or fulfillment.

global_hot_zones.issue: The two-staff enactment is followed by a second foolish-shepherd command and woe.
global_hot_zones.handling: Separate at 11:15 while preserving 11:4-17 as a paired-enactment alternative.

global_hot_zones.issue: Pouring, pierced-one wording, household lament, and fountain language invite identity and fulfillment judgments.
global_hot_zones.handling: Preserve the lament-to-fountain form across the chapter edge; decide no referent, identity, witness, reading, or fulfillment.

global_hot_zones.issue: The shepherd poem and opening day oracle can be adjacent units or one crisis movement.
global_hot_zones.handling: Separate at behold-a-day while recording the cross-chapter alternative; decide no chronology, identity, or fulfillment.

global_hot_zones.issue: Repeated in-that-day clauses link battle, altered day, waters, kingship, plague, pilgrimage, and holiness.
global_hot_zones.handling: Keep five refrain-governed movements under the full parent; adjudicate no history or eschatology.

units.title: Dated return summons and remembered response
units.literary_form: dated word-event exhortation with ancestral warning, rhetorical questions, and reported response
units.deciding_marker: The eighth-month date and word-event formula open the book; triple return language and questions about fathers and prophets resolve in a quotation of reconsideration before a new date at 1:7.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the summons from the ancestral questions or attaching it to the later night vision.
units.defensible_basis: Date change, repeated return formula, question sequence, and reported-response closure are directly visible form markers.

units.title: Night patrol, angelic lament, and comfort proclamation
units.literary_form: dated night vision with seeing, question, patrol report, intercession, and embedded oracle
units.deciding_marker: A second exact date opens a night vision; the what-are-these exchange advances through the patrol report and how-long appeal to a commanded proclamation whose repeated again language closes the episode.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating patrol, appeal, and proclamation into three chunks or merging the later horn vision.
units.defensible_basis: Date, vision report, question-answer chain, commissioned proclamation, and renewed lifting of the eyes at 1:18 bound and close the episode.

units.title: Four horns and four craftsmen
units.literary_form: compact vision with paired seeing reports and paired interpretation questions
units.deciding_marker: I-lifted-and-saw introduces horns; what-are-these receives an answer, then a second showing and what-are-these-coming-to-do exchange completes the two-part interpretation.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting horns from craftsmen despite the second image answering the first, or absorbing the measuring-line vision.
units.defensible_basis: Paired image-question-answer syntax and the fresh lifted-eyes report at 2:1 give a visible episodic frame.

units.title: Measuring line and unwalled city
units.literary_form: vision report with destination question and relayed angelic interpretation
units.deciding_marker: A fresh lifted-eyes formula introduces the measurer; where-are-you-going and the meeting of two angels lead to the run-and-speak commission ending in the wall-of-fire and inner-glory declaration.
units.rejected_alternative: Isolating the measuring question or merging the subsequent come/flee proclamation as though no form shift occurred.
units.defensible_basis: Fresh vision onset, destination question, relayed speech, and closure before the doubled imperative at 2:6 support the seam.

units.title: Flee, sing, and be silent
units.literary_form: imperative proclamation with escape summons, sending refrain, Zion song summons, and universal silence close
units.deciding_marker: Doubled come language and a direct flee command restart the discourse; sending-and-knowing language, sing-and-rejoice, dwelling promises, and be-silent-all-flesh carry it to a formal close.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating the flee summons, nations saying, Zion song, and silence command into isolated fragments.
units.defensible_basis: Imperative clusters, repeated sending/knowing refrain, vocative change, and terminal silence formula define one proclamation arc.

units.title: Joshua accused, reclothed, and turbaned
units.literary_form: courtroom-like vision and symbolic garment enactment
units.deciding_marker: The he-showed-me onset stages accuser, rebuke, filthy garments, removal, rich clothing, and clean turban as one completed transformation before a solemn assurance begins.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the rebuke from the garment enactment or treating the ensuing conditional charge as part of the physical action.
units.defensible_basis: Staged participants, sequential commands and fulfillment, and the new solemn-speech formula at 3:6 provide observable framing.

units.title: Solemn charge and sign saying to Joshua
units.literary_form: conditional commission expanding into a sign-oriented promise oracle
units.deciding_marker: The angel solemnly assures Joshua, moving from if-then commission to hear-now address, sign language, behold formulas, and the in-that-day vine-and-fig-tree closure.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating the conditional office charge from the sign saying or deciding identities named by the imagery.
units.defensible_basis: Solemn-speech onset, direct addressee continuity, if-then syntax, repeated behold, and in-that-day closure support the unit without interpreting identities.

units.title: Lampstand vision, embedded words, and olive-tree interpretation
units.literary_form: awakened vision with repeated questions, two embedded word-events, and resumed symbol interpretation
units.deciding_marker: The angel awakens the seer and asks what he sees; the lampstand description and what-are-these exchange embed words concerning Zerubbabel, then the doubled olive-tree question returns to the image and closes with an interpretation.
units.rejected_alternative: Extracting the embedded word-events as independent chunks and stranding the opening or resumed interpretation.
units.defensible_basis: Awakening frame, seeing question, recurring what-are-these exchange, embedded word-event, resumed questioning, and final answer preserve a single interlocked vision.

units.title: Flying scroll and house-entering curse
units.literary_form: vision with object-identification question and quoted interpretation
units.deciding_marker: Then-again-I-lifted introduces a flying scroll; dimensions answer what-do-you-see, and this-is-the-curse interpretation carries the image through its entry and destruction of houses.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the observed scroll from its interpretation or combining the following ephah vision.
units.defensible_basis: Fresh lifted-eyes onset, object question, this-is interpretation, and new angelic emergence at 5:5 clearly frame the episode.

units.title: Ephah, enclosed woman, and transport to Shinar
units.literary_form: vision with repeated object and destination questions, symbolic containment, and transport
units.deciding_marker: The angel comes forward with a lift-your-eyes command; what-is-it and where-are-they-carrying-it organize identification, containment, winged transport, and destination answer.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating identification and containment from the carrying scene or assigning theological identity to the figures.
units.defensible_basis: Angel emergence, seeing command, paired questions, continuous ephah referent, and destination answer make the movement self-contained.

units.title: Four chariots range through the earth
units.literary_form: final lifted-eyes vision with catalogue, interpretation question, dispatch, and quieting report
units.deciding_marker: Again-I-lifted opens the chariot catalogue; what-are-these leads to directional interpretation, the go-around command, fulfilled ranging, and a final called-out report about the north country.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting catalogue from dispatch or merging the renewed word-event sign-act at 6:9.
units.defensible_basis: Fresh vision formula, catalogue, interpretation question, command-execution sequence, and concluding report close the cycle-form episode.

units.title: Crowning sign-act and memorial oracle
units.literary_form: word-event command for a material sign-act with embedded oracle and conditional close
units.deciding_marker: A renewed word-event commands taking gifts, going the same day, making crowns, placing them, and speaking; the crowns become a memorial and the passage closes with a conditional diligently-obey clause.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting making and placement of crowns from the spoken oracle or deciding the referents and identities of the sign.
units.defensible_basis: Word-event onset, imperative chain, enacted object continuity, embedded saying formula, memorial function, and conditional closure supply a formal frame.

units.title: Dated fasting inquiry and motive questions
units.literary_form: dated delegation and cultic inquiry answered by rhetorical counterquestions
units.deciding_marker: A fourth-year date introduces the Bethel delegation and should-I-weep question; a word-event answers all people and priests with fast-for-me and eat-for-yourselves questions followed by an appeal to former prophetic words.
units.rejected_alternative: Isolating the delegation from the first response or extending through every later response in chapters 7-8.
units.defensible_basis: Exact date, delegation, explicit question, word-event response, paired rhetorical questions, and former-prophets closure establish an inquiry-answer unit.

units.title: Former command, refusal, and desolation
units.literary_form: renewed word-event with ethical command catalogue and retrospective refusal-consequence narration
units.deciding_marker: A renewed word-event restates commands, pivots with but-they-refused into a hearing refusal chain, and concludes with scattering and a desolate-land result.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating the command list from its refusal-consequence account or merging the new saying sequence at 8:1.
units.defensible_basis: Renewed word-event, command list, adversative refusal, call/refusal reversal, and causal desolation close are explicit discourse features.

units.title: Return to Zion and restored city scenes
units.literary_form: catena of divine sayings with jealousy onset, return declaration, paired street scenes, marvel question, and gathering promise
units.deciding_marker: A new word-event begins successive Yahweh-of-Armies-says panels; jealousy and return lead to old and young in the streets, a marvel question, and east-west gathering into Jerusalem.
units.rejected_alternative: Making each saying formula its own tiny unit or attaching the strong-hands exhortation at 8:9.
units.defensible_basis: Repeated saying refrain, linked Zion/Jerusalem setting, balanced street images, question-answer form, and completed gathering declaration create a coherent oracle sequence.

units.title: Strong hands, changed conditions, and truth-and-peace commands
units.literary_form: exhortation framed by oracle formulas, before-now contrast, fear refrain, and conduct catalogue
units.deciding_marker: Let-your-hands-be-strong opens a before-those-days versus but-now contrast; blessing reversal repeats do-not-fear and let-your-hands-be-strong, then these-are-the-things-you-shall-do supplies a closing command list.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting historical contrast, blessing promise, and conduct commands or absorbing the renewed fast word-event at 8:18.
units.defensible_basis: Opening and repeated strong-hands exhortation, temporal contrast, fear refrain, and explicit things-to-do catalogue frame the movement.

units.title: Fasts transformed and peoples seek Yahweh
units.literary_form: renewed word-event with transformed-fast declaration and escalating pilgrimage sayings
units.deciding_marker: A new word-event turns four fasts into feasts and commands love of truth and peace; yet-many-peoples then expands through city-to-city invitation to many peoples and ten-men imagery.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating the fast answer from the peoples-coming sayings or treating every oracle formula as an independent chunk.
units.defensible_basis: Renewed word-event, explicit fast answer, therefore command, repeated will-come movement, and climactic direct quotation provide closure to the dated inquiry complex.

units.title: Revelation over northern and coastal cities
units.literary_form: revelation/burden onset with geographic progression, city laments, remnant turn, and house-encampment close
units.deciding_marker: The revelation heading opens a place-name sequence from Hadrach and Damascus through Tyre-Sidon and Philistine cities; the movement closes with Yahweh encamped around his house and a now-I-have-seen formula.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at every named city or merging the new rejoice-greatly Zion address at 9:9.
units.defensible_basis: Burden heading, ordered geographic catalogue, stanza breaks, repeated city predications, and the first-person house-protection close frame the oracle.

units.title: Daughter Zion royal proclamation
units.literary_form: two-stanza acclamation and royal description with disarmament-peace scope
units.deciding_marker: Rejoice-greatly and shout address daughter Zion and Jerusalem, followed by behold-your-king; the next verse balances cut-off war instruments with speaking peace and a sea-to-sea closure.
units.rejected_alternative: Absorbing this compact acclamation into the city oracle before it or the prisoner address after it.
units.defensible_basis: New vocatives, acclamation imperatives, behold presentation, parallel royal predicates, and a complete dominion formula give the couplet coherence.

units.title: Prisoners of hope, battle manifestation, and flock salvation
units.literary_form: direct-address release oracle expanding into martial appearance and pastoral-crown closure
units.deciding_marker: As-for-you opens prisoner release and return commands; bow and sword imagery rises to Yahweh trumpet and defense, then in-that-day flock salvation and how-great exclamation close the sequence.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating prisoner restoration, battle imagery, and flock salvation into disconnected chunks.
units.defensible_basis: Direct-address onset, command and declaration chain, stanza progression, in-that-day turn, and terminal exclamatory abundance bind the movement.

units.title: Ask for rain; false guides and visited flock
units.literary_form: wisdom-like exhortation and false-guide indictment turning to shepherd judgment and battle simile
units.deciding_marker: Ask-of-Yahweh begins a rain exhortation contrasted with teraphim, diviners, dreams, and shepherdless wandering; therefore leads into anger against shepherds and a visited flock that becomes a battle horse.
units.rejected_alternative: Isolating 10:1-2 as a miniature saying or merging all restoration speech through 10:12.
units.defensible_basis: Imperative onset, for/therefore reasoning, shared flock-shepherd field, and complete visitation-to-battle turn support the larger unit.

units.title: Strengthening, gathering, return, and final strengthening
units.literary_form: first-person restoration oracle with repeated gather-bring language and inclusio
units.deciding_marker: I-will-strengthen opens the saying; strengthen, save, bring-back, signal, gather, sow, remember, return, and bring-again verbs carry it through geographic imagery to I-will-strengthen-them and a says-Yahweh close.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting Judah-Joseph promises from Ephraim joy or the gather-and-return sequence.
units.defensible_basis: First-person promise chain, repeated strengthening at both ends, gather/return lexical progression, and terminal speech formula create an inclusio.

units.title: Wail over fallen forest and ruined pride
units.literary_form: compact imperative lament with cascading tree, shepherd, and lion cries
units.deciding_marker: Open-your-doors and repeated wail imperatives move from Lebanon cedars through cypress and oaks to audible shepherd wailing and lion roaring.
units.rejected_alternative: Attaching the lament mechanically to the prior restoration oracle or to the prose feed-the-flock command without acknowledging the form break.
units.defensible_basis: Poetic formatting, imperative and wail refrain, descending natural imagery, and the prose command onset at 11:4 mark a discrete lament.

units.title: Feed the slaughter flock and break the two staffs
units.literary_form: commanded shepherd enactment with two named staffs, refusal speech, wage exchange, and paired break actions
units.deciding_marker: Feed-the-flock commands the action; first-person performance introduces Favor and Union, abandonment speech, breaking Favor, wage dialogue and throwing silver, then breaking Union completes the paired-staff enactment.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the two staffs, wage scene, and throwing action into unrelated chunks or merging the renewed foolish-shepherd command.
units.defensible_basis: Command-performance structure, first-person enactment sequence, named-object continuity, paired break actions, and new command at 11:15 delimit the unit.

units.title: Foolish shepherd equipment and terminal woe
units.literary_form: second shepherd sign command with explanatory oracle and woe closure
units.deciding_marker: Take-again explicitly restarts an enactment; for-behold explains the raised shepherd through neglected-flock and devouring clauses, ending in a woe and paired arm-eye curse.
units.rejected_alternative: Merging this second command into the two-staff enactment or isolating the final woe from its setup.
units.defensible_basis: Renewed command, explanatory for-behold, sustained shepherd field, and terminal woe formula provide a formal frame.

units.title: Jerusalem siege images and repeated in-that-day defense
units.literary_form: second revelation/burden onset with creator preamble, siege metaphors, chieftain speech, and deliverance refrain
units.deciding_marker: A new revelation heading and creator description introduce cup and burdensome-stone images; repeated in-that-day clauses move through horse panic, chieftain recognition, fire similes, saving tents, defending Jerusalem, and seeking destruction.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting every in-that-day saying or extending automatically into the lament beginning with I-will-pour.
units.defensible_basis: Burden heading, siege-image continuity, repeated temporal refrain, chieftain/inhabitant focus, and completed defense declaration support the larger movement.

units.title: Poured supplication, household lament, and opened fountain
units.literary_form: pouring declaration expanding into communal lament catalogue and in-that-day fountain close
units.deciding_marker: I-will-pour begins a new action and mourning response; as-one-mourns similes expand into great mourning and family-by-family apart repetition, followed by the in-that-day fountain announcement to the same houses and inhabitants.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at the chapter boundary, separating the household catalogue from the mourning onset, or deciding the identity and fulfillment of the pierced referent.
units.defensible_basis: Action-response onset, repeated mourning lexicon, catalogue refrain, shared addressees, and the following in-that-day cleansing image make the cross-chapter unit defensible as form only.

units.title: Removal of idols and discredited prophecy
units.literary_form: in-that-day removal oracle with hypothetical family speech, shame sequence, denial dialogue, and wound question
units.deciding_marker: It-will-come-to-pass-in-that-day opens removal of names, prophets, and impurity; when-anyone-still-prophesies leads through parental speech, prophetic shame, identity denial, and a closing question-answer about wounds.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the general removal oracle from the hypothetical dialogue or merging the distinct sword poem at 13:7.
units.defensible_basis: Temporal formula, repeated prophesy vocabulary, staged hypothetical dialogue, and poetry-form shift at 13:7 frame the unit.

units.title: Strike the shepherd and refine the remaining third
units.literary_form: three-stanza sword summons and flock-scattering poem with fraction and refining progression
units.deciding_marker: Awake-sword and strike-the-shepherd open a poetic command; scattering leads to two-parts/third-part contrast, then fire-refining, reciprocal calling, and paired people-God acclamations close the poem.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating shepherd striking from the two-thirds/one-third and refining stanzas or deciding the shepherd identity.
units.defensible_basis: Poetry shift, command onset, flock continuity, numerical progression, refining image, and reciprocal quotation close provide a complete stanza sequence.

units.title: The day comes: siege, battle, split mountain, and flight
units.literary_form: behold-day oracle with battle narrative, topographic transformation, flight command, and arrival close
units.deciding_marker: Behold-a-day opens gathering, siege, and city outcomes; then-Yahweh-will-go-out turns to battle, standing and splitting of the mountain, repeated you-shall-flee, and a final coming-with-holy-ones line.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting siege from mountain and flight or merging the altered-light saying without a seam.
units.defensible_basis: Behold-day onset, then progression, repeated battle/place vocabulary, flight refrain, and arrival closure define the movement without deciding chronology or fulfillment.

units.title: Unique day, living waters, kingship, and secure city
units.literary_form: in-that-day oracle sequence with altered-light riddle, water merism, kingship acclamation, and habitation close
units.deciding_marker: It-will-happen-in-that-day restarts with altered light and a unique day; living waters follow, then Yahweh-will-be-king and naming language lead to land transformation and Jerusalem dwelling safely.
units.rejected_alternative: Making each in-that-day saying independent or attaching the plague catalogue beginning at 14:12.
units.defensible_basis: Repeated temporal formula, day/light/water progression, royal acclamation, geographic description, and safe-dwelling closure bind the sequence.

units.title: Plague, panic, fighting, and camp animals
units.literary_form: plague catalogue with bodily triad, panic action, spoil notice, and animal extension
units.deciding_marker: This-will-be-the-plague introduces consuming flesh, eyes, and tongue; in-that-day panic, neighbor conflict, Judah fighting, gathered wealth, and a like-this animal plague complete the catalogue.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating bodily plague, panic, spoil, and animal extension or merging the survivors pilgrimage.
units.defensible_basis: Explicit plague onset, repeated consuming imagery, panic consequence, material spoil, and like-this extension to animals frame one catalogue.

units.title: Surviving nations annual worship and rain sanction
units.literary_form: survivor pilgrimage oracle with annual refrain, conditional cases, and summary sanction
units.deciding_marker: Everyone-left begins yearly ascent to worship and keep the feast; whoever-does-not-go introduces no-rain consequence, Egypt supplies a named conditional case, and this-will-be-the-punishment summarizes the rule.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the general pilgrimage from Egypt case or combining the holiness inscription closure.
units.defensible_basis: Survivor onset, annual worship refrain, conditional case pattern, and terminal summary sentence delimit the unit.

units.title: Holy bells, pots, and house closure
units.literary_form: in-that-day holiness expansion and terminal exclusion formula
units.deciding_marker: In-that-day introduces the bell inscription, compares temple pots to altar bowls, extends holiness to every pot in Jerusalem and Judah, and ends with a no-longer-in-the-house formula.
units.rejected_alternative: Treating the two closing verses as incidental residue or merging them into the pilgrimage sanction without preserving the all-holy climax.
units.defensible_basis: Temporal onset, repeated holy/house/pot vocabulary, expansion from inscription to every vessel, and book-final no-longer closure make this a distinct terminal movement.
